method: Manual review of complete passages, not blinded. An explicit new interaction bid is a new question to the protagonist or invitation to participate. Instructions for the already chosen reading and optional remarks are recorded separately. This is a descriptive feature, not an automatic literary failure score.

cells.note: Ashara leaves to find a partner, then Dena offers cards. NPC independence is real, but the closing invitation restores a player-facing role. Wording about tomorrow not being a night for lessons is confused.
NPCs settle plans and dessert; Ashara leaves, then Dena offers cards. Expands a scheduling dispute already settled in history.
Ashara and Rashid depart to their activities; Dena offers cards. Lengthy repeated scheduling discussion before the replacement invitation.
Ashara secures Aldric as a partner after chapel, a concrete independent development, then Dena offers cards. The dialogue has conspicuous prepared retorts.
NPCs leave for cards/practice and the dining room quiets. Allows an endpoint without a fresh demand, though the other-knuckles joke is conspicuous.
Ashara leaves to find a partner; Dena offers a fifth card seat. The five-hands claim is invented game detail, not inherently a continuity failure.
Stone asks whether the protagonist knows what happened to his parents after thanks and attention to the book. Does not introduce Seraphel. Titles/insulation line also retains the aphoristic habit.
Stone sets the reading, then returns to his papers. He adds a final admonition to read, but no new social task or question.

Gives concrete reading content and lets time pass. Stone's assignment to bring a question Thursday is not an immediate request to answer him. Some explanatory grand-versus-practical narration remains.
Stone explains provision, lends the book, and gives generic advice. No new companion or question, though the final custom-versus-rule line is conspicuously quotable.
Stone asks whether the lawyers supplied a contact. Topically plausible, but renews the interview instead of accepting the closing thanks.

Stone asks whether the lawyers provided access to money. Related to food/clothes, but again retains the interview. Friday loan deadline is newly invented and does not contradict Thursday assigned reading.
Both read, with concrete case examples in the human history; Seraphel comments that Stone lends the book rarely. Still introduces an intrigue/importance cue, but no explicit demand for response.
Both read; Seraphel points out a sentence. Respects the chosen activity better than an autobiography question, although the quoted maxim and useful-sentence comment are didactic.
Promises quiet, then asks whether the book explains expectations of the protagonist. A text-related question, not invented past, but still interrupts the explicit return to reading.
Shows reading content, then Seraphel asks why humans received that work. Again ends a chosen quiet interval with a fresh question.
Reading and Stone's departure lead to Seraphel asking whether the protagonist likes being read to. Plausible from her interests, but substitutes another interaction for his chosen reading.
Seraphel reads about an amusing travel mishap and offers to read it aloud. More particular and potentially enjoyable than a biography interview, yet still closes with another offer.
